# ZeroSound 0.11.4
- Replaces the pre-masked app icon with clean square source artwork so each macOS version can apply its native icon shape without clipped or doubled edges. - Keeps the connected-speaker identity clear at every ICNS resolution from 16 to 1024 pixels.

# ZeroSound 0.11.3
- Makes the complete room-health pill clickable, including its padding and chevron area.

# ZeroSound 0.11.2
- Uses the full available playout budget for packet reordering instead of declaring audio lost after a fixed 20 ms timeout. - Absorbs ordinary Wi-Fi latency bursts up to the real scheduling deadline while preserving the shared room presentation timeline. - Applies the same deadline-driven policy during playback startup, preventing a reordered first packet from producing an avoidable glitch. - Allows a bounded window of concurrent UDP submissions per receiver instead of serializing the audio stream behind completion callbacks and accidentally dropping packets locally. - Reports concealed audio as duration rather than packet count and distinguishes packets that arrived after their playback deadline. - Marks playback degraded only when concealment becomes audibly significant, while keeping minor handled network imperfections as technical telemetry. - Adds deterministic regression tests for 200 ms burst jitter, true packet loss, late arrival, continuous concealment, rolling telemetry, compatibility, and room-health behavior.

# ZeroSound 0.11.1
- Makes room health consequence-based: handled packet loss and reordering remain technical telemetry instead of producing false warnings. - Introduces clear Excellent, Stabilizing, Degraded, and Action needed states for current playback quality, automatic recovery, and failures that genuinely require intervention. - Prevents the health badge from oscillating while synchronization measurements settle or an audio path recovers. - Starts fresh playback telemetry for every stream generation and clears obsolete clock metrics when coordinator ownership changes. - Publishes empty renderer telemetry after playback stops, so an idle or recovered room cannot inherit missing-packet, underrun, resynchronization, or queue statistics from an earlier stream. - Preserves recovered timeouts as historical incidents without allowing them to degrade current room health. - Adds deterministic regression coverage for concealed loss, recovery, transport replacement, blocking failures, telemetry epochs, and health-state stabilization.

# ZeroSound 0.11.0
- Replaces shared UDP room traffic with ordered TCP control and a dedicated authenticated UDP audio and clock plane. - Makes joins explicit and bounded: partial joins clean up automatically and unsuccessful attempts return to discovery within five seconds. - Uses short-lived, atomically single-use UDP registration tokens so a stale or replayed endpoint cannot replace an authenticated member's current audio path. - Continuously reconciles every speaker against current packet room timestamps and the latest room clock, correcting hardware drift during playback instead of relying on the original anchor. - Uses bounded per-receiver audio sends so a slow Mac cannot create growing latency or stall another speaker. - Runs TCP room control, coordinator state, UDP routing, and member audio sockets on explicitly separated concurrency owners so audio pressure cannot stall membership or source changes. - Detects a silent or failed UDP path and replaces it through the existing authenticated TCP session without leaving or rejoining the room. - Keeps live audio isolated from unrelated members joining or leaving. - Recovers coordinator handoff through a fenced new term, survivor reconnect, clock relock, and fresh stream generation. - Expands diagnostics with control/audio transport state, join stage, before-send drops, clock skew, room-phase error, playback correction, and the last automatic recovery reason. - Adds deterministic fault simulations and real TCP/UDP integration coverage for rooms of up to eight Macs.
